sentences.text: The land bearing Survey No.41/3B of Sorakoppa Village, Bagalkote Taluk, was the land acquired under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
2. After negotiations between the land owner and the State, a consent award was passed on 25.10.1997.
The compensation is fixed in respect of the land, however, the valuation of the standing trees on the land acquired was not finalized.
Awaiting valuation of the standing trees from the competent authority, the award is passed fixing the compensation for the land acquired.
The award also stipulates that the supplementary award will be passed in respect of the standing trees after receipt of the valuation report.
3. Since the valuation was not fixed for the standing trees, Writ Petition is filed by the land loser seeking direction to fix the valuation for the standing trees on NC: 2023:KHC-D:10693 the land.
Writ Petition was allowed with a direction to determine the value of the standing trees.

4. Thereafter the valuation report is secured and based on the valuation report, the Special Land Acquisition Officer ('SLAO' for short) has passed a supplementary award fixing the valuation of the standing trees.

Aggrieved by the said valuation fixed by the SLAO in respect of the standing trees,
the land loser filed a Reference seeking enhancement of compensation.
5. The Reference Court accepted the plea of the claimant and awarded compensation for more trees than what is shown in the Joint Measurement Committee Report.
The Reference Court has allowed the petition and enhanced the compensation.
Aggrieved by the aforementioned judgment and award of the Reference Court, the State is in appeal.
Learned Government Advocate for the appellants submits that the award passed by the Reference Court is not tenable in law.

It is her contention that the Reference Court has erred in relying upon the concocted entries in the property records, which exaggerated the number of trees which in fact did not exist at the time of acquisition, as such, the judgment and award are liable to be set aside.

7. In support of her contention, learned Government Advocate would refer to the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in MFA No.100488/2014 (The State of Karnataka Vs. Smt.
Lakshmavva and Others) as well as in MFA No.100487/2014 (The Special land Acquisition Officer Vs. Shankrappa Akhandappa Goudar by his LRS).

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the claimant/respondent would submit that, in terms of the consent award passed in the first instance, the SLAO was required to pass an award in respect of the standing trees for which no NC: 2023:KHC-D:10693 award was passed when the compensation was determined in the first instance.

He would refer to the clauses in the said award, which would indicate that the compensation is not determined in respect of the standing trees and reference is made that the compensation will be awarded after securing the valuation report.
He would also submit that, in terms of the direction issued in the Writ Petition, the supplementary award is passed and compensation is ordered to be paid in respect of the 01 standing tree.

Aggrieved by the said award,
the land loser sought reference and placing reliance on the RTC, he claimed compensation for 46 trees and the Reference Court awarded compensation for 05 Ber trees, 40 Guava trees and 02 Mango trees.
9.
As can be noticed from the award which was initially passed by the SLAO, it is very much evident that the compensation was not determined in respect of the standing trees in the land acquired.
Thereafter, it NC: 2023:KHC-D:10693 was determined based on the valuation submitted by the competent authority.

However, the Reference Court on reference sought by the land loser, has placed reliance on the entries in the property records and awarded compensation for 05 Ber trees,
40 Guava trees and 02 Mango trees, as against the compensation awarded by the SLAO.
10. As can be noticed from the Joint Measurement Committee Report, there was only one standing tree when the land was acquired.
The subsequent entries in the Record of Rights reflecting the number of trees on the land acquired are not supported by any credible materials.
There is no credible evidence to disbelieve the Joint Measurement Committee Report.

This being the position,
the Reference Court erred in enhancing the compensation by awarding compensation for 46 additional trees.
The Reference Court could not have awarded compensation in respect of 46 trees.
Accordingly, the impugned judgment and award dated 27.03.2013 passed by the II Addl.
Senior Civil Judge, Bagalkot in LAC No.29/2013 are set aside.
Compensation fixed under the supplementary award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer is confirmed.
12. Appeal is allowed.
